first_proven_failure_boundary: The native Playwright action on the first #events article.event-card failed before scope choice. The receipt shows three cards, one picker host, a nonzero card rectangle, and elementFromPoint at the card center outside the card subtree. It does not identify the hit element or prove that the picker panel obstructed the action.
corroboration: Run 37284490515 also ended at select_B_card after the same-page A-to-B replacement, but its receipt did not record the failing operation.

hypotheses.candidate: The picker panel covers the Playwright click point.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Before-click center_hit_kind is picker_panel and card/panel rectangles intersect at the center.

hypotheses.candidate: The card center is outside the viewport or clipped.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Before-click center_in_viewport is false or all interior hit kinds are none while card geometry is nonzero.

hypotheses.candidate: Another page element covers the card or the layout changes during actionability checks.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Before-click hit kind is other_element, or before-click and after-failure hit kinds/rectangles differ.

instrumentation: Native receipt now preserves sanitized viewport/card/picker-panel rectangles and center/interior hit categories before the click and after failure. The receipt keeps only fixed categories and bounded numbers; no page text or raw Playwright error is stored.

focused_verification.scope: The actual page sampling callback was exercised with controlled DOM hit testing, plus receipt plumbing and allowlist. A scratch mutation dropping the pointer recording made the focused assertion fail. No native Chrome run or product behavior verified.

next_action: On an admitted native run using the changed driver, inspect before_click and after_failure pointer samples. Confirm the first causal boundary before changing driver click coordinates or picker layout; then prove a red/green behavioral guard against that cause.
